t: What Is a “Weyward” Macbeth? | Springer Nature Link
s: In most editions of [Macbeth], the witches refer to themselves as the “weird sisters” [see Figure S.1], and editors provide a footnote associating the word with Old English wyrd or “fate.” But we look in vain to the Folio for such creatures. Instead we encounter the “weyward Sisters” and the “weyard Sisters”; it is of “these weyward Sisters” that Lady Macbeth reads in the letter from Macbeth, and it is of “the three weyward sisters” that Banquo dreams.
